name: Square

webhook.algorithm: VERIFIED, and uniquely fragile — the signed payload includes something no other provider signs. Header `x-square-hmacsha256-signature`. HMAC-SHA256, base64, computed over `<notification URL> + <raw body>` — i.e. the exact configured notification URL is part of the signed string. Consequence PagoKit MUST generate correctly: the URL your app sees behind a proxy/tunnel (ngrok, load balancer, trailing slash difference) will not match the configured URL and verification fails with a correct secret. NO timestamp is signed — dedup on `event_id`. A `square-environment` header indicates sandbox vs prod

evidence.note: Catalog import from adversarially-checked research. The scheme above is quoted from that research and has NOT been transcribed into typed fields, so PagoKit will not generate a verifier. Promoting this provider to generic or build means reading the provider docs and typing the scheme in.

credentials.note: UNKNOWN. The commonly cited `EAAA…` access-token prefix and `sq0idp-` / `sandbox-sq0idb-` application IDs were NOT verified in this pass.

fees.notes: UNKNOWN — not verified this pass. Square publishes per-country rates that differ sharply between card-present and card-not-present; a single `card_domestic_pct` would be wrong for half of Square's use cases.

notes: The only entry here that unifies in-person (terminal/POS) and online payments under one API and one ledger. For a Claude Code user building for a physical business — a restaurant, a salon, a retail shop — Stripe Terminal is an add-on, whereas Square is the native answer. Also the only provider that natively settles Cash App Pay, which is material for US Gen-Z conversion. Ships an official MCP server.
SDKs: Official: Node `square`, Python `squareup`, PHP `square/square`, plus Java/.NET/Ruby and Web Payments SDK / mobile In-App Payments SDK.
Developer-experience scores are unrated placeholders (3/3); they are not used in ranking.
Overlaps: No overlap with any shipped provider on card-present. Overlaps stripe online-only.
Onboarding model was inferred during the catalog import and is not verified. Confirm it before relying on the "can this user actually get keys" filter.
